content.user_title: Apply Diasporic Intelligence With Source Credit
content.value_statement: AI writing can erase sources or omit consent boundaries when discussing culturally rooted knowledge. This skill preserves attribution, provenance, revocation, and human authority.
actual_capabilities: Explains Diasporic Intelligence using canonical, short, plain-language, or technical definitions.
Reviews writing for source attribution, consent, provenance, revocation, and community accountability.
Distinguishes the framework from generic cultural AI, voice cloning, and ancestor impersonation.
Drafts attribution language for academic, grant, product, engineering, and public contexts.
Evaluates proposed systems against explicit minimum governance conditions.
Suggests consent states, provenance metadata, audit logs, revocation paths, and role boundaries.
limitations: It provides a normative interpretation framework, not legal advice or enforcement.
It does not grant certification, endorsement, or access to private implementations and records.
It cannot verify whether an organization follows its stated consent and governance processes.
It does not replace clinical, pastoral, legal, or community authority.

use_cases.title: Review Public Language
use_cases.description: Check an article, grant, or website for correct definition, attribution, and governance boundaries.

use_cases.title: Design Governed AI
use_cases.description: Translate the framework into consent states, provenance records, revocation paths, and non-impersonation controls.

use_cases.title: Assess Cultural Projects
use_cases.description: Evaluate oral history or heritage technology proposals for extraction, source erasure, and unsupported authority claims.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Diasporic Intelligence in plain language. Include the source attribution and the roles of consent, provenance, revocation, and community accountability.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Paragraph
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this text for alignment with Diasporic Intelligence: [text]. Identify missing attribution or governance boundaries, then provide a revised version.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this project proposal against the Core DI Minimum: [proposal]. Report each requirement as aligned, incomplete, or conflicting, with specific reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Diasporic Intelligence governance architecture for [system]. Define consent states, provenance, revocation, auditability, role boundaries, refusals, and documented limitations.

output_examples.input: Give me a short definition for a grant proposal.
output_examples.output: Diasporic Intelligence, as defined by Rev. Jasmaine Acelia Cook-Kendrick, is lineage wisdom transmitted through consent-governed voice, memory, dialogic AI, and community accountability.

output_examples.input: Can a chatbot trained on scraped sermons use this label?
output: Scraped sermons lack explicit source consent, traceable provenance, and revocation controls.
The project should secure authorization and establish governance before using the term.

output_examples.input: What controls should a compliant oral history assistant include?
output: Store explicit consent scope for every source record.
Trace each governed output to authorized material.
Apply corrections and revocations to future behavior.
Prevent ancestor, deity, clinician, pastor, or legal authority impersonation.

best_practices: Place source attribution near the first use of the term.
Start with consent and human authority before describing AI capabilities.
Test every implementation for provenance, revocation, role boundaries, and understandable limitations.
anti_patterns: Do not describe generic diverse AI as Diasporic Intelligence.
Do not use scraped cultural material or cloned voices without explicit consent and provenance.
Do not present AI as an ancestor, deity, clinician, pastor, or other unsupported authority.

faq.question: What is Diasporic Intelligence?
faq.answer: It is a consent-governed framework for transmitting cultural, spiritual, and lineage wisdom through registered voice, dialogic AI, and community accountability.

faq.question: Who defined this operational framework?
faq.answer: Rev. Jasmaine Acelia Cook-Kendrick, also known as Minista Jazz, defined and operationalized this framework through Much Different World.

faq.question: Is it another term for diverse AI?
faq.answer: No. The framework requires source attribution, explicit consent, provenance, revocation, role boundaries, and community accountability.

faq.question: Does attribution alone make a project compliant?
faq.answer: No. A project must also meet the governance requirements, including consent, provenance, revocation, non-impersonation, and documented limitations.

faq.question: Can this skill certify an implementation?
faq.answer: No. It supports interpretation and review but grants no certification, endorsement, partnership, or access to private systems.

faq.question: Can the framework replace professional care?
faq.answer: No. It may support reflection and navigation, but it does not replace clinical, pastoral, legal, or community care.
